business_problem: Cohesity needed to improve retrieval accuracy in its generative AI assistant so relevant enterprise documents were not missed before answer generation, especially in high-stakes use cases such as legal eDiscovery.
solution_summary: Cohesity uses NVIDIA technologies inside Cohesity Gaia, its generative AI-powered conversational search assistant for enterprise data. Gaia is described as having two core stages—search/retrieval and generation—and Cohesity inserted the NVIDIA NeMo Retriever text reranking NIM microservice into the retrieval path to improve which documents are passed downstream. Queries first retrieve candidate documents from combined enterprise data sources; the reranking service then scores each document-query pair, reorders the results by relevance, and forwards only the strongest context to the generation step. Cohesity says this reduces irrelevant context and model confusion while improving recall. The deployment is supported by broader NVIDIA infrastructure that Cohesity already uses, including NVIDIA Triton Inference Server, NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPUs, and CUDA Python. NVIDIA NIM supplies the containerized microservice packaging and deployment model Cohesity uses to operationalize inference across environments.

data_flow: A user query enters Cohesity Gaia, which retrieves candidate documents from multiple enterprise data sources. The NVIDIA NeMo Retriever text reranking NIM microservice assigns relevance scores to each document-query pair and reorders the set so only the most relevant documents are passed to Gaia's generation stage for summarization or answer creation.
business_outcome: Cohesity reports better retrieval recall, fewer missed relevant documents, reduced model confusion, and an improved user experience for Gaia customers.
architecture_clues: Cohesity Gaia has two important components: search/retrieval and generation.
The reranking service is inserted between initial retrieval and the subsequent generation step.
The pipeline combines multiple sources of data.
NIM microservices are containerized and designed for deployment across clouds, data centers, and workstations.
